title: Domain case of henselian connectedness
statement: Let B be a commutative nonzero domain and let J be an ideal such that (B,J) is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Then the zero locus V(J) in Spec B [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is connected, including nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme], in its subspace topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.16 (Tag 09Y6, label lemma-irreducible-henselian-pair-connected, line 2948); 'connected' includes nonempty (Topology, Definition 5.7.1)

proof.text: The Jacobson condition of HenselianRing gives J ≤ Jac(B); since B is nonzero its Jacobson radical is proper. Thus B/J is nonzero. In Lean use Ideal.jacobson_eq_top_iff and Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.

For an idempotent e in B/J choose a representative a₀. For f=X(X-1), f(a₀) lies in J and f′(a₀) modulo J squares to 1, so it is a unit. HenselianRing.is_henselian lifts to a root a congruent to a₀. Since B has no zero divisors, a(a-1)=0 forces a=0 or 1. Therefore e=0 or 1. This works in characteristic 2 as well.

Apply the proved upstream PrimeSpectrum.connectedSpace_of_isIdempotentElem, using the clopen-idempotent criterion, to B/J. Its continuous image under comap of the quotient map is exactly V(J), by Mathlib range_comap_of_surjective and Ideal.mk_ker. IsConnected transports along continuous images and gives ConnectedSpace of the subtype.
